units.literal: Thereupon he secretly moved troops carrying rations, marched by forced marches on double routes, and raided their camp by night; the Xia people indeed collapsed in great disorder; they were pursued and killed for forty li, and those who fell from cliffs and ravines and died were beyond counting.

units.zh: 上聞之，賜金各五十兩、重幣十端，且詔諭曰：「卿等克成大功，朕聞之良喜。
units.en: When the emperor heard of it he rewarded each man with fifty taels of gold and ten bolts of heavy silk, and issued an edict: "You have won a great victory, and I am truly delighted.
units.literal: When the emperor heard of it he bestowed fifty taels of gold each and ten bolts of heavy silk, and also issued an edict saying: "You have achieved a great victory; I am truly delighted to hear it.

units.zh: 仍詔以合達之功遍諭河南帥臣。
units.en: An edict was also issued announcing Heda's achievement to all the commanders of Henan.
units.literal: An edict was also issued to announce Heda's achievement throughout to the commanders of Henan.

units.zh: 是月，與元帥買住又戰延安，皆被重創。
units.en: That month he fought again at Yan'an alongside Marshal Maizhu, and both were seriously wounded.
units.literal: That month he again fought at Yan'an together with Marshal Maizhu, and both suffered serious wounds.

units.zh: 十二月，以保延安功賜金帶一、玉吐鶻一，重幣十端。
units.en: In the twelfth month, for preserving Yan'an he was granted a gold belt, a jade gyrfalcon plaque, and ten bolts of heavy silk.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, for the merit of preserving Yan'an he was granted one gold belt, one jade gyrfalcon plaque, and ten bolts of heavy silk.

units.zh: 皆從之。
units.en: All of this was approved.
units.literal: All were approved.

units.zh: 經畫如此，彼當知畏，期之數年，卿等可以休息矣。」
units.en: With planning like this they should learn to fear us; in a few years you should be able to rest."
units.literal: With planning like this they should know fear; within a few years you should be able to rest."

units.en: The Wife of Zhong De
units.literal: Wife of Zhong De

units.zh: 蔡被圍，丁男皆乘城拒守，謂仲德曰：「事勢若此，丈夫能為國出力，婦人獨不能耶！」
units.en: When Cai was besieged and every able man manned the walls, she told Zhong De, "Matters stand as they do—if men can serve the state, why cannot women?"
units.literal: When Cai was besieged, all able-bodied men mounted the walls to resist; she said to Zhong De, "Affairs are thus—can a husband exert strength for the state while a woman alone cannot!"

units.zh: 完顏仲德妻，不知其族氏。
units.en: The wife of Wanyan Zhong De is a woman whose clan and surname are not recorded.
units.literal: The wife of Wanyan Zhong De—her clan and surname are unknown.

units.zh: 崔立之變，妻自毀其容服，攜妾及二子紿以采蔬，自汴走蔡。
units.en: During Cui Li's mutiny she disfigured her face and clothing, took a concubine and her two sons, disguised herself as a vegetable gatherer, and fled from Bian to Cai.
units.literal: In Cui Li's mutiny, the wife herself disfigured her face and dress, took a concubine and two sons, pretended to be gathering vegetables, and fled from Bian to Cai.

units.zh: 故太史公著《龜策》、《日者》及《扁鵲倉公傳》，皆所以廣其聞見，昭示後昆。
units.en: Hence Sima Qian’s treatises on tortoise divination, day-selection, and the physicians Bian Que and Lord Cang—all to widen what we know and guide posterity.
units.literal: Thus Grand Historian Sima Qian wrote the “Treatises on Tortoises and Divination,” “The Day Diviners,” and the “Biographies of Bian Que and Lord Cang”—all to broaden knowledge and show the way to later generations.

units.zh: 世宗第七子，母曰元妃李氏。
units.en: He was Shizong's seventh son; his mother was Yuan Consort Li.
units.literal: He was the seventh son of Shizong; his mother was Yuan Consort of the Li clan.

units.zh: 二十九年，世宗崩，章宗即位，進封潞王。
units.en: In year 29 Shizong died and Zhangzong took the throne; he was advanced to Prince of Lu.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Shizong died and Zhangzong ascended; he was advanced to Prince of Lu.

units.zh: 無何，章宗大漸，元妃李氏、黃門李新喜、平章政事完顏匡定策。
units.en: Soon Zhangzong was near death; Yuan Consort Li, palace attendant Li Xinxhi, and Grand Councilor Wanyan Kuang fixed the succession.
units.literal: Before long Zhangzong fell critically ill; Yuan Consort Li, Palace Attendant Li Xinxhi, and Grand Councilor Wanyan Kuang settled the plan.

units.zh: 衛紹王諱永濟，小字興勝，更諱允濟，章宗時避顯宗諱，詔改「允」為「永」。
units.en: Wei Shaowang—taboo name Yongji, childhood name Xingsheng, once taboo-named Yunji—during Zhangzong's reign, because of the taboo on Xianzong's name, received an edict changing "Yun" to "Yong."
units.literal: Wei Shaowang, taboo name Yongji, childhood name Xingsheng, formerly taboo-named Yunji; during Zhangzong's reign, to avoid Xianzong's taboo, an edict changed "Yun" to "Yong."

units.zh: 章宗崩，匡等傳遣詔，立衛王。
units.en: Zhangzong died; Kuang and his party passed on the final edict and set Prince Wei on the throne.
units.literal: Zhangzong died; Kuang and the others transmitted the death edict and enthroned Prince Wei.

units.zh: 既無繼嗣，而諸叔兄弟多在，章宗皆不肯立，惟欲立衛王，故於辭行留之。
units.en: He had no son, and many uncles and brothers still lived; Zhangzong would raise none of them, wishing only to make Prince Wei heir—so when Prince Wei tried to leave, he was kept back.
units.literal: With no heir of his own and many uncles and brothers still living, Zhangzong would establish none of them; he only wished to make Prince Wei his successor, and therefore detained him when he sought to leave.

units.zh: 而永蹈無後，乃以衛王子按陳為鄭王後，賜衛王詔曰：「朕念鄭王自棄天常，以幹國憲，槁瘞曠野，忽諸不祀。
units.en: Yongtao left no heir, so Prince Wei's son An Chen was made heir to Prince of Zheng. The edict to Prince Wei ran: "I think of Prince of Zheng, who threw away Heaven's law and breached the state's statutes, left to wither in the wild, and passed from sacrifice altogether.
units.literal: Yongtao had no heir, so the Prince of Wei's son An Chen was made successor to Prince of Zheng. An edict to Prince Wei said: "I reflect on Prince of Zheng, who abandoned Heaven's constants and violated state law, withered in burial on the open plain, gone suddenly without sacrifice.

units.zh: 歷歲既久，深用愴然。
units.en: Years have gone by, and grief weighs on me.
units.literal: Years have passed and I am deeply grieved.

units.zh: 親親之情。
units.en: Kinship tugs at the heart.
units.literal: The bonds of kin weigh upon me.

units.zh: 有懷難置。
units.en: I cannot set the feeling aside.
units.literal: My heart cannot find rest.

units.zh: 已詔追復舊爵，改葬如儀。
units.en: I have already ordered his old rank restored and a proper reburial.
units.literal: I have already ordered his former title restored and burial redone according to rite.

units.zh: 稽考古禮，以卿之子按陳為鄭王後，謹其祭祀，卿其悉之。」
units.en: By the ancient rites, your son An Chen is made heir to Prince of Zheng to keep his sacrifices—take full heed of this."
units.literal: Examining ancient rites, I make your son An Chen successor to Prince of Zheng to tend his sacrifices—see that you know this fully."

units.zh: 初，章宗誅鄭王永蹈、趙王永中，久，頗悔之。
units.en: At first Zhangzong had put Prince of Zheng Yongtao and Prince of Zhao Yongzhong to death; in time he came to regret it deeply.
units.literal: Initially Zhangzong had executed Prince of Zheng Yongtao and Prince of Zhao Yongzhong; after a long while he deeply regretted it.

units.zh: 是時，章宗已感嗽疾，衛王且辭行，而章宗意留之。
units.en: By then Zhangzong had fallen ill with a cough; Prince Wei was ready to depart, but Zhangzong meant to keep him at court.
units.literal: By then Zhangzong had contracted a coughing illness; Prince Wei was about to take leave, but Zhangzong intended to keep him.

units.zh: 宗章初年，雅愛諸王，置王傳府尉官以傳導德義。
units.en: Early in Zhangzong's reign he had loved his brothers dearly and set tutors and household officers in each prince's house to teach virtue.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhangzong's reign he had dearly loved the princes and appointed tutors and household officers in each princely establishment to convey moral teaching.

units.zh: 而衛王乃永蹈母弟，柔弱鮮智能，故章宗愛之。
units.en: Prince Wei was Yongtao's uterine younger brother—soft, ungifted, and mild—so Zhangzong held him dear.
units.literal: Prince Wei was Yongtao's younger brother by the same mother—gentle, weak, and little gifted—so Zhangzong favored him.

units.zh: 壬辰，章宗內人范氏損其遣腹，以詔內外。
units.en: On renchen Zhangzong's inner woman Fan injured the child she bore for him; an edict told the court and the realm.
units.literal: On renchen Zhangzong's inner attendant Fan harmed the pregnancy she was carrying for him; an edict announced this within and without.

units.zh: 初，章宗遣詔：「內人有娠者兩人，生男則立為儲貳。」
units.en: Earlier Zhangzong had sent an edict: "Two inner women are with child; whichever bears a son shall be made heir."
units.literal: Initially Zhangzong had issued an edict: "Among inner women, two are pregnant; if a son is born he shall be made heir."

units.zh: 四月庚辰，殺章宗元妃李氏及承御賈氏。
units.en: In the fourth month, on gengchen, Zhangzong’s Primary Consort Li shi and Palace Woman Jia shi were put to death.
units.literal: Fourth month, on gengchen, Zhangzong’s Primary Consort Li shi and Palace Woman Jia shi were killed.

units.zh: 《章宗實錄》詳其前事，《宜宗實錄》詳其後事。
units.en: The Veritable Record of Zhangzong treats the earlier reign; the Veritable Record of Xuanzong treats what followed.
units.literal: The Veritable Record of Zhangzong details earlier matters; the Veritable Record of Xuanzong details later matters.

units.zh: 十月，以前司農卿李渙飛語，詔左丞李蹊、戶部侍郎楊綎系獄，將以軍儲失計坐罪。
units.en: Tenth month: on former minister of agriculture Li Huan's whispered charges, an edict imprisoned left vice director Li Xi and vice minister of revenue Yang Shao for failure in military-store planning.
units.literal: Tenth month: on former Minister of Agriculture Li Huan's slander, an edict put Left Vice Director Li Xi and Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Shao in prison, to punish them for failure in military-store planning.

units.zh: 俄蹊、綎並除名，而止籍綎家貲。
units.en: Soon Xi and Shao were both struck from the rolls; only Shao's household goods were inventoried.
units.literal: Soon Xi and Shao were both struck from the rolls; only Shao's household goods were registered.

units.zh: 以右丞相、樞密使兼左副元帥賽不，平章政事、權樞密使兼右副元帥白撒，右副元帥兼樞密副使權參知政事訛出，兵部書權尚書左丞李蹊，元帥左監軍行總帥府事徒單百家等率諸軍扈從。
units.en: Saibu, right chief councillor, privy councilor, and left vice marshal; Ba Sa, chief councillor, acting privy councilor, and right vice marshal; Echu, right vice marshal, privy vice commissioner, and acting participation councillor; Li Xi, acting minister of war and acting left vice director; Tushan Baijia, left marshal-inspector and acting headquarters commander, and others led the escort.
units.literal: Saibu, right chief councillor and privy councilor and concurrent left vice marshal; Ba Sa, chief councillor and acting privy councilor and concurrent right vice marshal; Echu, right vice marshal and privy vice commissioner and acting participation councillor; Li Xi, acting minister of war and acting left vice director of the Masters of Writing; Tushan Baijia, left marshal-inspector acting headquarters commander, and others led the armies in escort.

units.zh: 又神農、桐君論《本草》藥性，黃帝、岐伯說病候治方，皆聖人之所重也。
units.en: Shennong and Lord Tong classified herbs in the Root Canon; the Yellow Emperor and Qibo set forth disease and cure—all arts the sages held dear.
units.literal: Again, Shennong and Lord Tong discussed the properties of drugs in the Root Canon of Materia Medica; the Yellow Emperor and Qibo explained symptoms and healing prescriptions—all were prized by sages.

units.zh: 正大元年正月戊戌，諡大行皇帝曰繼天興統述道勤仁英武聖孝皇帝，廟號宣宗。
units.en: On the wuxu day of the first month, Zhengda 1, the late emperor received the posthumous title Emperor Jitian Xingtong Shudao Qinren Yingwu Shengxiao, with the temple name Xuanzong.
units.literal: On the wuxu day of the first month of the first year of Zhengda, the late emperor was given the posthumous title Emperor Jitian Xingtong Shudao Qinren Yingwu Shengxiao, with the temple name Xuanzong.

units.zh: 天興元年春，大兵駐鄭州海灘寺，遣使招哀宗降。
units.en: In the spring of Tianxing 1, the Mongol army encamped at Haitansi in Zheng Prefecture and sent envoys urging Emperor Aizong to surrender.
units.literal: In the spring of the first year of Tianxing, the Great Army encamped at Haitansi in Zheng Prefecture and sent envoys to summon Emperor Aizong to surrender.

units.zh: 冬十月，哀宗議親出捍禦，以奴申參知政事、兼樞密副使，完顏習捏阿不樞密副使、兼知開封府、權參知政事，總諸軍留守京師。
units.en: In the tenth month of winter, Emperor Aizong planned to lead the defense in person. He left Nushen as vice grand councilor and concurrent vice commissioner of military affairs, and Wanyan Xinie Abu as vice commissioner of military affairs, concurrent prefect of Kaifeng, and acting vice grand councilor, to command all forces and hold the capital.
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Emperor Aizong deliberated going out in person to resist; he made Nushen Vice Grand Councilor and concurrent Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Wanyan Xinie Abu Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, concurrent Prefect of Kaifeng, and Acting Vice Grand Councilor, to command all armies and remain to guard the capital.

units.zh: 完顏奴申，字正甫，素蘭之弟也。
units.en: Wanyan Nushen, courtesy name Zhengfu, was the younger brother of Suluan.
units.literal: Wanyan Nushen, styled Zhengfu, was the younger brother of Suluan.

units.zh: 天興二年正月丙寅，省令史許安國詣講議所言：「古者有大疑，謀及卿士，謀及庶人。
units.en: On bingyin day in the first month of Tianxing 2, secretariat clerk Xu Anguo went to the deliberation office and said: "In antiquity, when grave doubts arose, counsel was sought from ministers and nobles, and from the common people as well.
units.literal: On the day bingyin in the first month of the second year of Tianxing, Secretariat clerk Xu Anguo went to the Deliberation Office and said: "In antiquity, when there was great doubt, counsel was sought from ministers and nobles, and counsel was sought from the common people.

units.zh: 左右司官因奏把撒合、石魯亦宜任用，上曰：「世達曲從，非出得已，然朕猶少降資級，以示薄罰。
units.en: The left and right bureau officials memorialized that Basage and Shilu should also be employed. The emperor said: "Shida bent to circumstances—not willingly—yet I still lowered his rank slightly to show a light punishment.
units.literal: The left and right bureau officials thereupon memorialized that Basage and Shilu should also be employed; the emperor said: "Shida bent to follow—not of his own free will—yet I still slightly lowered his rank to show a light punishment.

units.zh: 彼撒合掌軍一面，石魯宿衛九重，崔立之變，曾不聞發一矢，束手於人。
units.en: Basage commanded one sector of the army and Shilu guarded the palace. At Cui Li's mutiny neither loosed a single arrow and both submitted helplessly.
units.literal: Those two—Basage commanding one face of the army, Shilu guarding the ninefold palace—at Cui Li's mutiny never so much as loosed a single arrow and submitted helplessly to others.

units.zh: 今雖來歸，待以不死，足以示恩，又安得與世達等？
units.en: Now that they have returned, sparing their lives is grace enough. How can they be treated like Shida?
units.literal: Now though they have come back, to spare their lives is enough to show grace—how can they be treated like Shida and the others?

units.zh: 撒合老矣，量用其子可也。
units.en: Basage is old; employing his son will suffice.
units.literal: Basage is old; it is enough to employ his son in measure.

units.zh: 石魯但當酬其負禦容之勞。」
units.en: Shilu need only be rewarded for carrying off the imperial portraits."
units.literal: Shilu need only be rewarded for the labor of carrying the imperial portraits."

units.zh: 詔諭近臣曰：「尉忻資稟純質，事可倚任，且其性孝，朕今相之，國家必有望，汝輩當效之也。」
units.en: An edict told the close ministers: "Weixin's character is pure and solid and he may be relied upon in affairs. Moreover he is filial. I now make him councilor—the state must have hope. You should take him as your model."
units.literal: An edict instructed the close ministers: "Weixin's endowment is pure and solid; in affairs he may be relied upon, and moreover his nature is filial. I now make him councilor—the state must have hope; you should take him as your model."

units.zh: 汴受圍數月，倉庫匱乏，召武仙等入援不至，哀宗懼，以曹王訛可出質，請罷攻。
units.en: Kaifeng had been under siege for months, and the granaries were empty. Wuxian and others were called to relieve the city but never came. In fear, Emperor Aizong offered Prince Cao, Eke, as a hostage and asked that the assault be halted.
units.literal: Bian had been besieged for months; storehouses were exhausted; Wuxian and others were summoned to relieve the city but did not arrive; Emperor Aizong was afraid and offered Prince Cao, Eke, as hostage, requesting that the attack cease.

units.zh: 哀宗北禦，以孤城弱卒托之奴申、阿不二人，可謂難矣。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong went north to resist the invaders, entrusting a besieged city and a feeble garrison to Nushen and Abu alone, the task was formidable indeed.
units.literal: When Emperor Aizong went north to resist, entrusting a lone city and weak troops to Nushen and Abu alone, it may be called difficult indeed.

units.zh: 乃梟立首，望承天門祭哀宗。
units.en: They displayed Cui Li's head on a pole, faced the Gate of Receiving Heaven, and offered sacrifice to Emperor Aizong.
units.literal: They then displayed Li's head on a pole, faced the Gate of Receiving Heaven, and offered sacrifice to Emperor Aizong.

units.zh: 哀宗遷歸德，天驥留汴中。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained in Kaifeng.
units.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained in Bian.

units.zh: 哀宗欲修宮室，尉忻極諫，至是臥薪嚐膽為言，上悚然從之。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong wished to repair the palace buildings, Weixin remonstrated fiercely, even invoking the example of sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall. The emperor was startled and complied.
units.literal: Emperor Aizong wished to repair the palace buildings; Weixin remonstrated to the utmost, even speaking of sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall; the emperor was startled and complied.

units.zh: 哀宗為太子，有定策功，由是頗惑其言，複倚信日深，台諫每以為言。
units.en: When Emperor Aizong was crown prince, Sagelian had helped settle the succession. For this reason the emperor was much swayed by his words and relied on him ever more deeply. The censorate often remonstrated about this.
units.literal: When Emperor Aizong was crown prince, he had the merit of settling the succession; for this reason he was much swayed by his words, and reliance and trust grew daily deeper; the censorate often spoke of it.

units.zh: 哀宗終不能去。
units.en: In the end Emperor Aizong could not remove him.
units.literal: Emperor Aizong in the end could not remove him.
